Rumors of the foldable iPhone Ultra are just weeks away from launch. As we've written before, anticipation for this new device continues to build.

Bloomberg published a new report today outlining what Apple employees who have tried the iPhone Ultra like most about it.

iPhone Ultra is coming: real-world impressions

In the latest edition of the Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman provided an in-depth recap of the foldable iPhone. He specifically mentioned that he "spoke with several people," and the things they liked most after testing the device include:

  • How pocketable it is. It's rumored to feature a 5.5-inch outer display.
  • The durability of the hinge.
  • A new "iPad-like app layout" that makes full use of the inner display, which is reportedly around 7.8 inches with a landscape orientation wider than tall.
  • Its performance as a "camera viewfinder."

Multiple reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will be priced over $2,000. It's expected to feature main and ultrawide cameras, but no telephoto lens. Touch ID is reportedly set to replace Face ID as the biometric authentication method.

9to5Mac's take

I'm incredibly excited about the iPhone Ultra, and these details from Gurman make me even more optimistic that this is the right device for me.

I was originally skeptical about the form factor of a foldable iPhone, but as we've learned more about its specific dimensions and advantages, I've changed my mind.

The positive reception of Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 also provides valuable real-world reference for a form factor extremely similar to the iPhone Ultra.

Of course, it will come with certain limitations compared to the iPhone 18 Pro. I'm currently using an iPhone Air, so I'm already accustomed to life without a telephoto lens, and going back to Touch ID wouldn't be too big of a transition for me either.

What are your thoughts on the iPhone Ultra rumors? Will you be picking one up this fall? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
